discovery.about: obscura: a headless browser engine in Rust (a fork carrying local patches) with real V8 JavaScript, its own DOM, layout and CPU paint, a Chrome DevTools Protocol server for Puppeteer and Playwright, an MCP server and a stealth mode, aimed at scraping and AI-agent automation.
discovery.see: Project overview: comparison with headless Chrome, installation from releases, Docker and source, quick start for fetch, dumps, screenshots and private-network testing, native rendering, the CDP server and parallel scrape, Puppeteer and Playwright examples, benchmarks, stealth mode, the CDP API table, CLI reference and MCP setup.

Stealth mode in the README: building with render and stealth, anti-fingerprinting measures (per-session fingerprint values, userAgentData, isTrusted events, hidden internals, native function masking, webdriver) and the 3,520-domain tracker blocking.
Table of implemented Chrome DevTools Protocol domains and methods (Target, Page, Runtime, DOM, Network, Fetch, Storage, Input and others) for Puppeteer and Playwright compatibility.

Guidance for agents and contributors: build commands per feature set, cargo nextest instead of cargo test, the 33-stage obstacle course gate, the finish checklist, crate architecture, performance and panic-safety conventions, rendering verification, gotchas, robustness invariants and stealth scope.

AAS V2.0 binding form of AGENTS.md: build, test, finish gates, architecture, conventions, rendering verification, gotchas and robustness invariants as kernel laws, with the rule that a conflict between the two files is a defect.

Contribution guide: code of conduct, what to check before starting, building, testing with nextest, rendering change methodology with fixtures and real-site captures, the pre-PR checklist, commit message and pull request style, reporting bugs, project scope and license.

Security policy: private reporting through GitHub advisories with an email fallback, what to include, response process, in-scope issues (SSRF egress, availability, memory safety, data integrity, TLS identity) and exclusions, dependencies, the watchdog and egress security model, and supported versions.

Workspace manifest: the ten member crates, shared dependency versions (html5ever, selectors, taffy, tiny-skia, tokio, reqwest without cookies), patches to vendored taffy and cosmic-text with their reasons, panic = unwind required for op panic safety, and the release-dist profile.
Multi-stage Docker build: compiles the workspace in rust slim with dependency caching via stub crates, then ships obscura and obscura-worker on a distroless nonroot runtime image.
cargo-deny policy: ignored unmaintained-crate advisories (fxhash, paste, rustybuzz, ttf-parser) with reasons, duplicate version warnings and the allowed license list.

Agent skill for operating and validating Obscura: build variants, using stealth, fetching, evaluating and capturing, driving CDP and MCP, validating visual behavior against fixtures and real sites, and setting expectations accurately about rendering limits.
Dependency-free Node script that streams what an obscura serve browser shows to a local browser tab by adaptively polling Page.captureScreenshot, so you can watch an agent session live.

The published documentation: installation and first fetch, data and markdown extraction, connecting Puppeteer and Playwright with detailed guides, the MCP server and live session viewing, the Rust library, request interception, cookie and storage persistence, stealth and proxies, production operations, CLI and environment variable references, architecture, extension recipes and testing and debugging.

The workspace crates: obscura-cli (fetch, serve, scrape, mcp, worker), obscura-cdp (DevTools Protocol server and domains), obscura-mcp (agent tools), obscura-browser (Page, contexts, PDF), obscura-js (V8 runtime, bootstrap.js, ops), obscura-dom (tree, parser, selectors), obscura-net (HTTP and stealth clients, cookies, blocklist), obscura-render (cascade, layout, text, paint), obscura-ssrf and the obscura library API.

Rendering verification harness: about 70 deterministic HTML fixtures for floats, flex, grid, tables, positioning, replaced elements, forms, fonts, transforms, media emulation and print, run.sh and check.py for paired Obscura versus Chromium captures with checks.json expectations, and a representative real-site suite driven by paired-corpus.py.
Readme of the vendored taffy flexbox and grid layout library, which the workspace patches in place of the crates.io release to carry a grid shrink-to-fit correction until it lands upstream.
Readme of the vendored cosmic-text shaping library, patched locally (per Cargo.toml) to carry canonical variable-font coordinates through shaping and rasterization.

GitHub bug report form: preflight checks, version or commit, platform, how obscura is used (CLI, CDP, MCP, library), affected area, build features and stealth, reproduction, expected and actual behavior, rendering details with a Chrome comparison, and logs.
